sections.html: Schistura notostigma remains small, around 5-6 cm. It is a peaceful omnivore with no special requirements in terms of water composition.
In the wild, these animals usually live in shallow water (around 3 cm) in running waters with a pebble bottom.
The temperature can be between 22 and 26°C. The species is adaptable and does not need a strong current, but a certain flow in the tank should be a matter of course for such fish.

All three loaches are peaceful, but create a small territory around a cave. This can be under a stone, a root or something else. A pair likes to move in here. S. notostigma should always be kept in a group so that the exciting social behaviour of these fish can be observed.
The males are strongly yellowish in color, the females have a red belly (animals apparently in spawning mood).

Until recently this species was thought to be the only Schistura species from Sri Lanka, but recently two other species have been described from there, S. madhavai and S. scripta. The easiest way to distinguish the three species is by the stripes on the forebody. S. madhavai is unstriped in front of the dorsal fin, S. notostigma has 6-7 broad stripes in front of the base of the anal fin towards the head and S. scripta has 7-13 narrower stripes. S. notostigma also differs from S. scripta in having a complete lateral line (incomplete in S. scripta, ending below the dorsal fin). Unfortunately, this can hardly be seen in live animals.
